pageCache.pageTitle: Torfield - World Book Day at Torfield - News - Torfield and Saxon Mount Academy Trust
pageCache.text:
Torfield - World Book Day at Torfield
Each term at Torfield, our children enjoy lessons based around a carefully chosen text. This ensures all our pupils benefit from accessing high quality literature across a broad range of genres, including fiction, non-fiction, poetry and plays.
While most texts are set each year, we always leave one term’s choice open so that our school community can select a book they feel is important for our pupils to enjoy.
Last year, we chose a new book, The Café at the Edge of the Woods by Mikey Please, and we are proud to see that it was such a hit in our school that one pupil chose to celebrate World Book Day by coming to Torfield dressed as Glumfoot, one of its characters. Another pupil chose to dress as Hilda from Luke Pearson’s Hilda and the Hidden People. This was an exciting choice, as it is a new book we do not yet have in school—and it may even become one the children study next year.
Today’s optional costume day has been just one part of our week long World Book Day celebrations at Torfield. Other activities have included book hunts around the school, tours of book themed classroom doors and, of course, lots and lots of opportunities to enjoy books and reading!
Executive Headteacher / CEO Miss. A Jagot

pageCache.pageTitle: Torfield - Dance Showcase 2026 - News - Torfield and Saxon Mount Academy Trust
pageCache.text:
Torfield - Dance Showcase 2026
This week, we ended the term in style with our annual Dance Showcase, where each class took to the stage to share the dance techniques they’ve been developing in their PE lessons. It was a wonderful opportunity for pupils to perform, celebrate their hard work, and enjoy the excitement of presenting their learning to an audience.
From our younger learners exploring simple rhythm and movement, to our older pupils demonstrating more complex choreography and control, the showcase highlighted the clear progression of skills throughout the school. Watching how pupils’ coordination, confidence and creativity have grown from year group to year group was truly impressive.
The atmosphere was full of energy and enthusiasm, and it was fantastic to see children taking part, supporting one another, and showing pride in what they have achieved. Events like this not only celebrate physical education but also help pupils develop teamwork, resilience and a love of performing.
Executive Headteacher / CEO Miss. A Jagot

pageCache.pageTitle: Torfield - Circus Skills - News - Torfield and Saxon Mount Academy Trust
pageCache.text:
Torfield - Circus Skills
Don’t worry – we haven’t posted this picture upside down! This week, pupils from Oceania Class took part in an exciting and highly active circus skills workshop, giving them the opportunity to try a range of new physical activities in a fun, inclusive environment.
Led by experienced instructors, the session introduced pupils to a variety of circus disciplines and each activity was carefully adapted to ensure that all children could participate, succeed and be challenged at their own level.
The workshop broadened our pupils’ experiences of physical activity beyond traditional sports by exploring alternative movement skills, pupils developed key aspects of being active, such as balance, coordination, agility and core strength — all essential foundations for lifelong participation in physical activity.
Importantly, the session also promoted confidence, resilience and perseverance. Pupils showed great determination as they mastered techniques that were completely new to them.
The pupils thoroughly enjoyed the experience and left feeling proud of their achievements — and perhaps a little like circus stars themselves!
Executive Headteacher / CEO Miss. A Jagot

pageCache.text:
Torfield - Safer Internet Day
To mark Safer Internet Day, all pupils have taken part in age and stage appropriate lessons and activities focused on using the internet safely. A key theme this year has been the safe and responsible use of AI, helping pupils understand both the opportunities and the potential risks associated with new technologies.
At Torfield, we recognise that keeping children safe online is a vital part of our safeguarding role. Online safety is therefore taught regularly throughout the school year, not just on Safer Internet Day. Pupils are supported to use technology safely, responsibly and confidently as part of their everyday learning.
To help you continue these conversations at home, class teachers will be sharing class specific ideas and resources on Class Dojo. Please remember that if you ever need support or advice, particularly around setting up safety controls on new devices, staff at Torfield are always available to help.

pageCache.text:
Saxon Mount - Year 8 trip to Rye Harbour Nature Reserve
Year 8 went on a hunt for treasure amongst the pebbles at Rye Harbour Nature Reserve.
Staff from Sussex Wildlife Trust were enthusiastic as they talked about the important wildlife site which is home to more than 4000 'species of plants and animals, including 300 that are rare or endangered'.
Pupil's explored the different items that might wash up on beaches as flotsam and jetsam, and the many different types of shells that they may find.
The highlight of the day seemed to be watching the big trucks and bulldozers moving the shingle after recent storms.

pageCache.text:
Saxon Mount - Tchoukball and Cricket
Year 10 PE lessons are the best!
With Tchoukball inside, students had the opportunity to engage in a fast-paced, team-oriented sport that emphasises cooperation and strategy over aggression. This unique game, often described as a blend of handball and volleyball, encourages players to think on their feet and work together to score points by rebounding the ball off a frame. Once outside, the focus shifted to cricket, a classic sport that combines skill, patience, and teamwork. It was a great way for students to enjoy the fresh air and sunshine while honing their batting, bowling, and fielding skills. A great way to end the day, a sunny and energetic Monday filled with fun and sport!

Torfield - From a 'wasteland' to a garden.
“It’s gone from a wasteland to a garden” – Torfield School Councillor
Last year, our School Council played a key role in helping to decide the features of our new outdoor learning space. Today, they visited the area to see the elements they had chosen and to plan the next stages of the space’s development.
The changes we have made to this part of Torfield mean that all of our classes have been able to access outdoor learning throughout the winter. Now that spring is here, we are enjoying the opportunity to observe the changes of the season and look forward to a summer of inclusive outdoor education at Torfield.
